(ANSA) - ROME, 18 NOV - General-turned politician Roberto Vannacci's far-right National Future (FnV) party is being probed for allegedly reconstituting Mussolini's banned Fascist Party after a complaint from a military trade union, judicial sources said Wednesday. Following a formal complaint filed by the Military Personnel Union—which suggested that the party might be in violation of the Scelba Law regarding the reconstitution of the Fascist Party—the Rome Public Prosecutor's Office has opened a "Model 45" file (a register for documents that do not constitute evidence of a crime), reported la Repubblica online. According to the Rome-based newspaper, the document submitted by the Union requests an investigation into whether FnV replicates "the anti-democratic doctrinal core and the methods of struggle" characteristic of Fascism. Vannacci's lawyer said the accusations against the party were inconsistent, even for the investigators. "We have, as always, full confidence in the judiciary. We are pleased to learn that the Rome Prosecutor's Office has registered the Military Union's complaint in Form 45, the register of documents not constituting a crime. It is therefore reasonable to assume that, at this stage, the accusations appear inconsistent, even to investigators," said Giorgio Carta, lawyer for MEP Vannacci. "We have not yet had the opportunity to read the complaint, however, given how they have been reported in the press, we believe the accusations to be completely unfound
